title: The Protocol of Kepler Reach
premise: Emrys Ishikawa has spent nine years alone at Kepler Reach, tending Earth's abandoned seed vault and recording the slow decay of a colony that stopped answering. When the ship Meridian returns from deep space carrying a crew who have aged backward into youth, Emrys discovers they were sent to retrieve a memory-erasure protocol the colony's founders used to bury an original sin: Kepler Reach was never a seed vault, but a prison for minds extracted from dying colonists. As the returned crew's memories begin reasserting themselves, Emrys must carry the truth to the relay at the edge of dead space before the corporation that built the Reach can purge it again — choosing between broadcasting the archive (and destroying the imprisoned minds she has come to love) or letting the lie stand. She broadcasts it, sacrificing her own recorded years to give the prisoners their names back.
about_author: Elodie Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete agricultural data before turning to fiction. She writes quiet, melancholy science fiction about people left behind by progress.

chapters.title: The Last Inventory
chapters.summary: Emrys records her 3,287th daily log in the silent seed vault, cataloguing failing systems and the colony dome that went dark years ago. Her only companions are the seeds and a half-functional caretaker AI. The beat is loneliness worn smooth into ritual — until a light appears on the horizon where nothing should be.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: A ship lands at the dead colony. Its crew is impossibly young — faces Emrys recognizes from colony portraits, aged backward decades. Their captain, Sefa Okonkwo, claims they've been gone eleven months. Emrys's POV; the beat is uncanny dread braided with desperate hope that someone finally came back.

chapters.title: What the Seeds Remember
chapters.summary: Emrys shows the crew the vault; Sefa reacts with recognition she shouldn't have, humming a lullaby native to the colony. Emrys realizes the crew's bodies are young but something older lives in them. POV alternates as Sefa begins dreaming in memories that predate the mission. Beat: creeping wrongness.

chapters.title: The Founders' Floor
chapters.summary: Investigating the sealed sublevel beneath the vault, Emrys finds rows of dormant pods — not seeds, but neural archives, human minds stored after the colony's 'evacuation.' One pod holds a mind that signs its dreams with Emrys's mother's name. Beat: the floor drops out of everything she believed.

chapters.title: Sefa Remembers Dying
chapters.summary: Sefa's suppressed memories surface violently: she recalls the evacuation, the corporation's extraction teams, her own death of radiation sickness — and waking here. She confronts Emrys, accusing the vault of being a lie. Emotional beat: grief and fury colliding into fragile alliance.

chapters.title: The Protocol
chapters.summary: In the founders' records, Emrys finds the truth: the Meridian was sent by Halcyon Combine to retrieve and destroy the extraction protocol evidence before the relay's legal disclosure deadline. The crew are living proof, meant to be reclaimed. Beat: cold clarity — they are all evidence now.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Logs
chapters.summary: Emrys plays the crew her nine years of recordings: the colony's slow death, her solitary vigils, the voices she heard in the vault's static. Sefa realizes the 'static' was the archived minds speaking to the one person who kept listening. Beat: devastating tenderness; Emrys was never alone, just unheard.

chapters.title: Halcyon Answers
chapters.summary: A corporate retrieval ship enters orbit, demanding the crew's return and the vault's 'decommissioning.' Emrys stalls via comms while Sefa plans. The beat is claustrophobic pressure — the race structure ignites, and the relay at the edge of dead space becomes the only exit.

chapters.title: Stealing the Meridian
chapters.summary: The crew hijacks their own ship from the retrieval team under cover of a dust storm, Emrys abandoning the vault she swore to keep. She carries one seed case and the protocol data. Beat: exhilaration shadowed by guilt — the caretaker leaving the garden burning.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: The crossing to the relay through signal-dead space, where the archived minds aboard grow louder without interference. Emrys begins hearing her mother clearly for the first time. Quiet chapter; beat: intimacy with the dead, love forming against every duty she was given.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Young
chapters.summary: Crewmember Dev Anand's re-aged body begins failing — the reversal was never stable. His death forces the crew to face that they are on borrowed time, and that Halcyon may have designed them to expire. Beat: mortality made urgent; the clock tightens.

chapters.title: Intercept
chapters.summary: Halcyon transmits an offer: return the crew, receive restored original bodies and full pardons — except Emrys, who will be erased as a rogue archivist. Sefa nearly accepts. Beat: betrayal's edge, then refusal; Sefa chooses the woman who listened over the company that made her.

chapters.title: Mother Static
chapters.summary: Emrys confesses what the pod-mind told her: her mother wasn't evacuated — she volunteered for extraction to stay near the vault, and has been the static in Emrys's logs for nine years. Beat: the book's emotional core; love and grief fused, duty to the dead reframed as love against duty.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: They reach the ancient relay station, derelict and barely powered. Bringing the transmitter online requires someone to interface directly with the archived minds — risking the same dissolution. Emrys volunteers; Sefa refuses to let her go alone. Beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Disclosure Deadline
chapters.summary: Halcyon's fleet arrives in-system; the legal window to broadcast closes in hours. Inside the interface, Emrys navigates the archive's cathedral of stored minds, finding thousands of colonists who chose imprisonment over true death. Beat: awe and horror entwined; the scale of the crime revealed.

chapters.title: What the Archive Wants
chapters.summary: The archived minds vote: some want erasure as mercy, most want broadcast — to be named, mourned, remembered, even if it ends them. Emrys's mother asks her daughter to be the one who speaks. Beat: consent and agency; the prisoners reclaim power from their jailers.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Under fire from Halcyon's boarding teams, Sefa holds the relay while Emrys transmits the full protocol, the names, and nine years of logs across settled space. The cost: the transmission draws its power from the archive itself, and from Emrys's recorded memories. Beat: triumphant, terrible sacrifice.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: The broadcast ripples outward; colonies that forgot Kepler Reach wake to their own stolen history. Halcyon's ships withdraw as public outrage detonates. Emrys wakes remembering her childhood but not her nine years — the price paid. Beat: hollowed victory, dawn after a long night.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: The surviving crew and freed archive-minds hold a memorial at the relay, reading the names of the extracted dead. Emrys listens to strangers tell her who she was for nine years. Beat: mourning transformed into inheritance; memory restored by community when personal memory fails.

chapters.title: The Return Voyage
chapters.summary: The Meridian turns home toward a changed system, carrying the last seed case. Sefa and Emrys navigate what they are to each other now — not rescuer and rescued, but partners who chose each other over every protocol. Beat: quiet love, unforced, earned.

chapters.title: Kepler Reach, Replanted
chapters.summary: They return to the vault, now a pilgrimage site. Emrys plants the first external garden in the colony's history, her mother's voice present in the wind rather than the static. Beat: healing without forgetting; the caretaker becomes the gardener.

chapters.title: Log Entry, Day One
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Emrys begins a new log series — not recording a death this time, but a beginning. She addresses future listeners, promising to keep the record honest no matter who holds power. Final beat: vigilance as devotion; memory entrusted forward, the story closing on an open channel.
